feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 0 (4 cm row, +/-0.02 m) had the best progress, 0.185 on the s-bend, but 2 line-loss events per s-bend and slalom run. Iteration 1 (2 cm row, +/-0.03 m) reduced s-bend line loss to 1 but cut s-bend progress to 0.04, so the row position and the controller changes together are the likely cause. The next race is the test: if s-bend progress recovers toward 0.185 while line loss stays at or below 1, keep the 4 cm row and change only the body. If progress stays low, return the body to 0.18 m and 0.8 kg to separate the effects. The rule for the outer sensors is also the same: keep 15 mm spacing and symmetric weights, because I have had to raise kp to match the lower signal per metre.
requested_changes: If s-bend progress is at or above 0.15 and line_loss_events is at or below 1: keep sensor_positions at y=0.04 with x from -0.03 to 0.03, and try sensor_size 0.016 to cover more tape at the edges. Evidence: iteration 0 (y=0.04) gave progress 0.185; iteration 1 (y=0.02) gave 0.04 with line loss halved.

If progress is below 0.10 on the s-bend while line loss stays low: revert body_length to 0.18 and mass to 0.8, keeping the spread and row, to test whether the lighter body caused the drop. Evidence: iteration 1 progress fell to 0.04 with no change to body geometry, which suggests the sensing changes were the main cause, so the body change must be checked separately.

If steering_oscillation stays above 0.15 on the slalom while rms_error is below 0.03: move the row to y=0.03 as a compromise between the 4 cm and 2 cm lookahead. Evidence: iteration 0 oscillation was 0.163 on the slalom at y=0.04, and iteration 1 oscillation was 0.155 at y=0.02, so the lookahead alone did not clearly control jitter.
